description: AI video/image ad-generator SaaS for Balkan COD e-commerce

_auditConfigComment: Two advisories `pnpm audit` reports that DO NOT APPLY here, verified against the
lockfile BEFORE silencing them. Both are Remotion criticals whose stated range is
<4.0.410; the only `remotion` in pnpm-lock.yaml is 4.0.490. The tell is in the audit
output itself: every genuine finding prints a dependency Paths chain, and these two
print an EMPTY Paths - pnpm could not resolve them to anything installed and reported
WARNING: only ever add a GHSA here that has been checked against the LOCKFILE, with the
reason written down. An entry justified by 'it was noisy' is how a real advisory gets
silenced. If Remotion is ever downgraded below 4.0.410, DELETE both entries - they
would then be hiding a live RCE.
_overridesComment: Security overrides, added 2026-08-18 after the CI security job's first run. Each one
forces a transitive dependency past a published advisory that no direct upgrade
reaches, because the vulnerable copy is pulled by next, cheerio or @remotion/bundler
undici is why this was done now rather than 'later': cheerio uses it to fetch URLs the
CUSTOMER supplies via /api/scrape - the same surface that produced five SSRF spellings
in safe-url.ts - so an outdated HTTP client sits directly on it.
WARNING 1 - ranges are CARET-pinned to the major the consumer declares, never a bare
>=. The first attempt used >=7.29.0 for undici and pnpm resolved 8.10.0, while cheerio
declares ^7.19.0 - a major swapped underneath the library that fetches customer URLs.
No unit test would catch that: the scraper's tests mock the fetch.
WARNING 2 - these live HERE and not in pnpm-workspace.yaml with the older overrides.
pnpm 10.0.0 applied the package.json ones and did NOT apply the same entries written
in the yaml (sharp stayed 0.34.5 there and moved to 0.35.x here). Verify any change by
reading pnpm-lock.yaml, never by trusting 'Already up to date'.
